title: Canonical sequence-to-intake migration inventory
summary: The canonical registry contains 27 sequences, not two wrappers. The migration surface includes commit/push, deployment/database operations, container and workflow drivers, authentication and user administration, package/setup scripts, cleanup, discovery controllers, convergence controllers, and a live workflow-resume driver. A no-argument executable is not automatically compliant: several scripts immediately execute defaults, others print usage, and others still require the model to construct argv, JSON files or strings, environment assignments, stdin, or MCP objects.

migration_summary.compatibility_rule: Legacy arguments remain only for grounded machine callers; normal skill/sequence use routes through no-argument intake.

evidence_index.limitations: Registry prose does not prove source behavior.

Installed skill matches the argument-bearing source skill.
Prototype requires format/example/constraints and builds typed answers/argv.
evidence_index.limitations: Prototype covers only two callers and still exposes generic argv collection.
